newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk combine, gas supplier to merge.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk combine, gas supplier to merge.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel flagship metals combine and its energy supplier, Norilskgazprom, will merge in a move aimed at resolving the two companies' deep financial troubles, a senior bankruptcy official said on Friday.
Pyotr Mostovoi, general director of the Federal Bankruptcy Administration, told a news conference that Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin's bankruptcy commission had approved the scheme.
"The only decision that will effectively solve the financial problems of both companies is a speedy merger," he said, adding that the two companies would issue shares.
It was not clear if this meant that the Norilsk unit, which officials have said in the past is not immune from bankruptcy, was now in fact not a potential candidate for liquidation.
The Norilsk Mining and Metals Enriching Complex is a subsidiary of RAO Norilsk Nickel, one of the world's largest producers of nickel, copper, cobalt, platinum and platinum group metals.
Norilskgazprom is one of the few natural gas entities in Russia that is not part of the natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom.
Norilskgazprom supplies 90 percent of its production to Norilsk Nickel, and the two companies are in a cycle of inter-enterprise debt with each other.
Mostovoy said both companies needed to lower their expenses and resolve social-spending issues, and said the companies, not the government, were responsible for this.
He did not name the size of the companies' debts, but said the Norilsk Nickel combine and Norilskgazprom were Russia's second and fourth largest debtors, respectively.
"This decision (to merge) seems tough, but we have no alternative and we submit to it," RAO Norilsk Nickel general director Alexander Khloponin told the same news conference.
He said the scheme for the merger was still not clear and declined to comment further.
He put Norilsk Nickel's debts to the federal budget, not including fines, at 500 billion roubles.
Potanin's press secretary, Larisa Zelkova, said documents authorising the merger could be ready within a month.
